# Why do we have Requirements

In order to ensure a minimum level of quality of the components available in the Central Repository, we have established a number of requirements your deployment components have to meet. This allows your users to find all the relevant details about the components from the metadata provided in the Central Repository.

## Supply Javadoc and Sources[⚓︎](#supply-javadoc-and-sources "Permanent link")

Projects with packaging other than `pom` have to supply JAR files that contain Javadoc and sources. This allows the consumers of your components to automatic access to Javadoc and sources for browsing as well as for display and navigation.

For every `<artifactId>-<version>.jar` file, you must provide a corresponding `<artifactId>-<version>-sources.jar` and a `<artifactId>-<version>-javadoc.jar`. While we do not attempt to evaluate the javadoc contents or the source code itself, we suggest that you provide accurate sources and comprehensive documentation. This will assist your component's users to make effective use of your library.

If you cannot provide sources or documentation, we allow uploading placeholder `.jar` files in order to pass validation. We suggest that you include a `README.md` file in the `.jar` that directs the user to where they can get further information about your project.

## Provide File Checksums[⚓︎](#provide-file-checksums "Permanent link")

All files deployed need to have valid checksum files (containing hex-encoded checksum value):

-   `.md5` and `.sha1` are required,
-   `.sha256` and `.sha512` are supported but not mandatory.

E.g. if you deploy the files:

`example-application-1.4.7.pom example-application-1.4.7.jar example-application-1.4.7-sources.jar example-application-1.4.7-javadoc.jar`

you need to include the files:

`example-application-1.4.7.pom.md5 example-application-1.4.7.pom.sha1 example-application-1.4.7.jar.md5 example-application-1.4.7.jar.sha1 example-application-1.4.7-sources.jar.md5 example-application-1.4.7-sources.jar.sha1 example-application-1.4.7-javadoc.jar.md5 example-application-1.4.7-javadoc.jar.sha1`

and you can include the files:

`example-application-1.4.7.pom.sha256 example-application-1.4.7.pom.sha512 example-application-1.4.7.jar.sha256 example-application-1.4.7.jar.sha512 example-application-1.4.7-sources.jar.sha256 example-application-1.4.7-sources.jar.sha512 example-application-1.4.7-javadoc.jar.sha256 example-application-1.4.7-javadoc.jar.sha512`

## Sign Files with GPG/PGP[⚓︎](#sign-files-with-gpgpgp "Permanent link")

All files deployed need to be signed with GPG/PGP and a `.asc` file containing the signature must be included for each file. E.g. if you deploy the files:

`example-application-1.4.7.pom example-application-1.4.7.jar example-application-1.4.7-sources.jar example-application-1.4.7-javadoc.jar`

you need to include the files:

`example-application-1.4.7.pom.asc example-application-1.4.7.jar.asc example-application-1.4.7-sources.jar.asc example-application-1.4.7-javadoc.jar.asc`

If you need more help setting up and configuring GPG, please read our [detailed instructions](gpg/).

Notice that `.asc` files don't need checksum files, nor do checksum files need `.asc` signature files.

## Required POM Metadata[⚓︎](#required-pom-metadata "Permanent link")

As part of your deployment, you are required to submit a `pom` file. This is the *Project Object Model* file used by Apache Maven to define your project and its build. When building with other tools you have to assemble it and ensure it contains the following information.

Besides the required information we strongly recommend you include the correct dependencies of your project. Build tools can use that information to resolve transitive dependencies correctly and your users will not be required to manually manage the dependencies.

### Correct Coordinates[⚓︎](#correct-coordinates "Permanent link")

The project coordinates, also known as GAV (group, artifact, version) coordinates, determine the location of your project in the repository. The values are:

-   `groupId`: the top level namespace level for your project starting with the reverse domain name
-   `artifactId`: the unique *name* for your component
-   `version`: the version string for your component

The version can be an arbitrary string but cannot end in `-SNAPSHOT`, since this is the reserved string used to identify versions that are currently in development. However we strongly suggest that you use \[semantic versioning\] [http://semver.org](http://semver.org) to assist your users in their version choices.

A valid example is:

`<groupId>com.example.applications</groupId> <artifactId>example-application</artifactId> <version>1.4.7</version>`

In addition your project needs to specify `packaging` unless your project is being published with the default `jar` packaging. Example packaging values are `jar` , `war` ,`ear` , `pom` , `maven-plugin` , `ejb` , `rar` , `par` , `aar` and `apklib` with other values being valid as well.

### Project Name, Description and URL[⚓︎](#project-name-description-and-url "Permanent link")

We require the presence of `name` , `description` and a `url` for more, human readable, information. For example:

`<name>Example Application</name> <description>A application used as an example on how to set up pushing   its components to the Central Repository.</description> <url>http://www.example.com/example-application</url>`

A common and acceptable practice for `name` is to assemble it from the coordinates using Maven properties:

`<name>${project.groupId}:${project.artifactId}</name>`

### License Information[⚓︎](#license-information "Permanent link")

You need to declare the license(s) used for distributing your components. E.g. if you use the Apache License you can use:

`<licenses>   <license>     <name>The Apache License, Version 2.0</name>     <url>http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt</url>   </license> </licenses>`

Another example is the MIT license:

`<licenses>   <license>     <name>MIT License</name>     <url>http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php</url>   </license> </licenses>`

### Developer Information[⚓︎](#developer-information "Permanent link")

Developer information is also required:

 `<developers>     <developer>       <name>Manfred Moser</name>       <email>manfred@sonatype.com</email>       <organization>Sonatype</organization>       <organizationUrl>http://www.sonatype.com</organizationUrl>     </developer>   </developers>`

It is acceptable to link to your profile on GitHub or other repository hosting providers if you do not have a website.

### SCM Information[⚓︎](#scm-information "Permanent link")

The connection to your source control system is another required element. The syntax used depends on the version control system used. `connection` details the read only connection, while `developerConnection` details read and write access connection details. The `url` contains the URL for a web front-end to your SCM system.

Note

While these elements are required, the URL itself does not need to be public. You can specify a URL inaccessible to the public or even a placeholder noting that your SCM URL is private and not meant for public access.

Detailed information is available in the [Maven SCM documentation](http://maven.apache.org/scm/) for [various supported formats](http://maven.apache.org/scm/scms-overview.html) and a number of common examples follow.

Subversion on your own server:

`<scm>   <connection>scm:svn:http://subversion.example.com/svn/project/trunk/</connection>   <developerConnection>scm:svn:https://subversion.example.com/svn/project/trunk/</developerConnection>   <url>http://subversion.example.com/svn/project/trunk/</url> </scm>`

Git hosted on GitHub:

`<scm>   <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/simpligility/ossrh-demo.git</connection>   <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://github.com:simpligility/ossrh-demo.git</developerConnection>   <url>http://github.com/simpligility/ossrh-demo/tree/master</url> </scm>`

Git hosted on BitBucket:

`<scm>   <connection>scm:git:git://bitbucket.org/simpligility/ossrh-pipeline-demo.git</connection>   <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://bitbucket.org:simpligility/ossrh-pipeline-demo.git</developerConnection>   <url>https://bitbucket.org/simpligility/ossrh-pipeline-demo/src</url> </scm>`

Mercurial on BitBucket:

`<scm>   <connection>scm:hg:http://bitbucket.org/juven/hg-demo</connection>   <developerConnection>scm:hg:https://bitbucket.org/juven/hg-demo</developerConnection>   <url>http://bitbucket.org/juven/hg-demo</url> </scm>`

Git on Apache Git Server from Apache Maven:

`<scm>   <connection>scm:git:https://git-wip-us.apache.org/repos/asf/maven.git</connection>   <developerConnection>scm:git:https://git-wip-us.apache.org/repos/asf/maven.git</developerConnection>   <url>https://github.com/apache/maven/tree/${project.scm.tag}</url>   <tag>master</tag> </scm>`

## A Complete Example POM[⚓︎](#a-complete-example-pom "Permanent link")

The following complete example shows the XML header and required elements of `project` and `modelVersion` as well as example elements and content.

`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">   <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>    <groupId>com.simpligility.training</groupId>   <artifactId>ossrh-demo</artifactId>   <version>1.0</version>   <packaging>jar</packaging>    <name>ossrh-demo</name>   <description>A demo for deployment to the Central Repository via OSSRH</description>   <url>http://github.com/simpligility/ossrh-demo</url>    <licenses>     <license>       <name>The Apache Software License, Version 2.0</name>       <url>http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt</url>     </license>   </licenses>    <developers>     <developer>       <name>Manfred Moser</name>       <email>manfred@sonatype.com</email>       <organization>Sonatype</organization>       <organizationUrl>http://www.sonatype.com</organizationUrl>     </developer>   </developers>    <scm>     <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/simpligility/ossrh-demo.git</connection>     <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://github.com:simpligility/ossrh-demo.git</developerConnection>     <url>http://github.com/simpligility/ossrh-demo/tree/master</url>    </scm>  ...  </project>`

These are the requirements for the `pom` file. We discourage the usage of `<repositories>` and `<pluginRepositories>`, instead publish any required components to the Central Repository. This applies for your own components as well as for 3rd party artifacts.

Fully configured example projects including metadata as well as dependencies and Maven build configuration are available at:

<!-- Maven 3.10 writes a `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each
                     artifact dir in the staging; Central rejects a bundle with
                     content that isn't a `.pom`. Strip them before the Central
                     plugin builds the bundle (this plugin must be declared BEFORE
                     central-publishing-maven-plugin so its `deploy` step runs
                     first). -->
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-antrun-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.1.0</version>
                    <executions>
                        <execution>
                            <id>strip-central-staging-metadata</id>
                            <phase>deploy</phase>
                            <goals><goal>run</goal></goals>
                            <configuration>
                                <target>
                                    <delete quiet="true">
                                        <fileset dir="${session.executionRootDirectory}/target/central-staging"
                                                 includes="**/maven-metadata-*.xml" />
                                    </delete>
                                </target>
                            </configuration>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>
                <!-- Uploads the whole reactor to the Sonatype Central Portal as one
                     deployment (auto-published after validation). Credentials come
                     from the `central` server in ~/.m2/settings.xml. -->
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.sonatype.central</groupId>
                    <artifactId>central-publishing-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>0.6.0</version>
                    <extensions>true</extensions>
                    <configuration>
                        <publishingServerId>central</publishingServerId>
                        <autoPublish>true</autoPublish>
                    </configuration>
                </plugin>

- name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
          cache: maven
          server-id: central
          server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
          server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
          gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE

      # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
      # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
      # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
      # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
      - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          v=3.9.9
          curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
          echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          mvn -v

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      - name: Download the platform natives
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: natives

      - name: Stage the natives for the jar embed
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native
          for d in natives/native-*; do
            platform="${d#natives/native-}"
            mkdir -p "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform"
            cp "$d"/* "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform/"
          done
          find lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native -type f

      # The demos are excluded from the release reactor: central-publishing-maven-plugin
      # bundles every reactor module (it ignores maven.deploy.skip), and the demos must
      # not be published.
      - name: Deploy to Maven Central
        working-directory: lib/java

          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: >-
          mvn -B -P release deploy
          -pl '!pathland-demo-views,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'

The runner image `20261004` moved `ubuntu-latest` to **Maven 3.10.0**, which writes a **`maven-metadata-local.xml`** beside each artifact in the Central staging (`org/pathland/<artifact>/maven-metadata-local.xml`). `central-publishing-maven-plugin` bundles it, and the Portal rejects the bundle: *"content that does NOT have a .pom file: org/pathland/…"* (all 14 artifacts, including `pathland-parent`, whose only artifact is its POM). Fixes a shadow added via a modifier not appearing in the SSR HTML (it only showed up after hydration), and aligns the SSR's `box-shadow` order with the browser.

## 1. Radius-only shadow wasn't drawn
The DSL's `shadow(radius)` (a `Shadow` modifier without an explicit color) emits **only `SHADOW_RADIUS`** — the color is renderer-owned. The HTML renderer required **both** `SHADOW_RADIUS` and `SHADOW_COLOR`, so it dropped the shadow in the SSR. After hydration the DOM client draws it (defaults the color to `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)`), which is why it "appears once hydrated".

**Fix:** draw the `box-shadow` when `SHADOW_RADIUS` is non-zero **or** there is an `SHADOW_X`/`SHADOW_Y` offset, using `SHADOW_COLOR` when set and the renderer default `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)` otherwise — mirroring the DOM client.

## 2. `box-shadow` order
The SSR wrote `box-shadow:<x>px <y>px <radius>px <color>`, but a browser serializes a `box-shadow` back as `<color> <x>px <y>px <radius>px` — so pre- and post-hydration strings differed (rendering was identical). Emit the **color first** in both the HTML renderer and the DOM client's `recomposeShadow`, so the SSR string matches the hydrated DOM.

- New unit test `shadow_renders_with_a_renderer_default_color_when_only_radius_is_set` (radius-only → default color; offset-only → draws; unset/zero → none; explicit color wins). `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` → 70 pass.

690: ### SizeThatFits — `SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17
691: 
692: A **fit slot**: it shows **one child at a time — the currently selected
693: candidate**. In the **live (delta) form** only that child is ever transmitted:
694: the app owns the candidates (their views never ride the wire) and transmits the
695: **fit query** (`FIT_QUERY`, LIST — the candidates' `minWidth` thresholds,
696: ascending) plus the selected child. In a **full-snapshot emission** (the web SSR
697: first document), every candidate is transmitted as a child — the renderer renders
698: all branches and the browser selects the matching one (see the visibility
699: contract below) so the first paint is already correct. The renderer measures its
700: **own allocated width** (the slot is size-taking — it stretches to its parent's
701: proposal, never hugs, so it always has a well-defined width) and selects the fit
702: **locally**:
703: 
704: > **Fit rule** — the selected index is `max{ i : thresholds[i] ≤ measured
705: > width }` (threshold 0 candidate always qualifies — the fallback); equal
706: > thresholds pick the **lower index**; before the first measure the app renders
707: > the threshold-0 candidate (index 0). The measurement is in **logical points**,
708: > so the pick is identical on every renderer given the same slot width.
709: 
710: The renderer reports its selection back with **`FIT_CHANGED`** ([EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md))
711: — emitted **once after the first measure, and then only when the derived fit
712: index changes** (a band crossing). It never streams the raw size. The app reacts
713: by swapping the slot's child (a `TREE` delta pair); a selection that maps to the
714: already-shown view re-emits **zero** opcodes. After a **full-snapshot**
715: presentation (all candidates laid out), the first `FIT_CHANGED` is the signal
716: that collapses the slot back to the live single-selected-child form.
717: 
718: **Candidate identity (MUST).** The candidate **index `i`** is the candidate's
719: position in the **ascending `FIT_QUERY` table** (equal thresholds keep the app's
720: surface order). In a **full-snapshot emission** the slot's **child order MUST
721: equal `FIT_QUERY` order** — the child at position `i` is candidate `i`. The fit
722: rule, the `FIT_CHANGED` payload, and the CSS gate all use this one mapping. A
723: candidate declared first in the DSL but carrying a **higher** `minWidth` is
724: therefore **not** index 0.
725: 
726: **Full-snapshot visibility (MUST).** In a full-snapshot emission the renderer
727: MUST show **exactly one** candidate — the one at `index(w)` for the slot's own
728: allocated width `w` — with no JS:
729: 
730: - the slot's own width is the query context (each slot is measured
731:   independently);
732: - each candidate is gated behind a marker carrying its `FIT_QUERY` index;
733: - for every threshold `T_i` with `i ≥ 1` there is a **band** that, at
734:   `w ≥ T_i`, makes candidate `i` visible and **hides every candidate `j ≠ i`**;
735:   bands are emitted **ascending** so the highest matching band wins; no band
736:   exists for `T_0`;
737: - the per-candidate **default** (below the first band / no match) is candidate
738:   `0` visible, every other candidate hidden;
739: - **invariant**: exactly one candidate is visible at every width.
740: 
741: **Hydration collapse (MUST).** After the first `FIT_CHANGED` the app swaps the
742: slot to the live single-selected-child form (the unselected candidates leave as
743: `TREE` deltas) and the renderer removes the full-snapshot gating — the gate
744: markers, the query context, and the band rules — so no CSS gate remains; a
745: `FIT_CHANGED` that maps to the already-shown candidate re-emits **zero** opcodes.
746: 
747: The collapse is signalled by the **removal of a candidate** (a `TREE` `REMOVE_CHILD`
748: /`DELETE_NODE` on the slot), not by an arbitrary structural op. A **full-snapshot
749: emission replayed as opcodes** (e.g. `META::RESYNC`) therefore does **not** collapse
750: the slot: the renderer reuses its existing gate (the SSR gate markers + band rules)
751: and keeps showing the width-correct candidate. The app's retained tree stays in the
752: snapshot form until the first `FIT_CHANGED` downgrade actually removes a candidate.
753: 
754: The concrete web realization (CSS container + per-candidate gate wrappers +
755: `@container` band rules) is **renderer-owned** and described in
756: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`.
757: 
758: Semantics:
759: - **Properties**: `FIT_QUERY` (`0x1039`, LIST).
760: - **Events**: `FIT_CHANGED` (`0x13`, host → guest) — reported fit index.
761: - **Children**: at most one in the live form; all candidates in a
762:   full-snapshot emission (the web SSR's first document), in `FIT_QUERY` order.
763: - **Renderer statelessness**: the measured width and derived index are layout
764:   output, not retained application state.

I've mapped the whole SizeThatFits path. Here's my analysis and a debugging plan.

## What "all branches rendered" actually is

A `SizeThatFits` slot in the **SSR first document** is a *full-snapshot* slot: it emits **every** candidate, each wrapped in `<div data-pathland-fit-cand="i">` (candidate 0 `display:contents`, the rest `display:none`), and the slot becomes a CSS container (`container-type:inline-size; container-name:pf-<id>`). A `<style data-pathland-fit>` in the head holds `@container pf-<id> (min-width:T){…}` **band rules** that flip exactly one candidate visible. So before hydration the *only* thing hiding the losers is that CSS gate.

The gate is meant to be torn down exactly once, when the app **downgrades** the slot (N→1) on the first `FIT_CHANGED`:
- App (`Emitter.reconcileSlot`, `Emitter.java:439-468`) keeps the selected candidate, emits `REMOVE_CHILD`+`DELETE_NODE` for the losers.
- Client (`apply.ts:456` → `collapseFitSlotFor`, `apply.ts:1434-1459`) **unwraps every `data-pathland-fit-cand` wrapper, strips `container-type`/`container-name`/`data-pathland-fit-cands`, and drops the slot's band rules** — then relies on the app's `REMOVE`/`DELETE` deltas to delete the losers.

If the gate is torn down but the losers are **not** all removed, every candidate is a plain visible child → **all branches rendered** (permanent, until a later same-component fit swap morphs the slot back to one child).

## Leading hypotheses (why a rotate triggers it)

1. **The teardown is too eager and not atomic (top suspect).** `apply.ts:456` fires on *any* `REMOVE_CHILD`/`DELETE_NODE` whose `closest("[data-pathland-fit-cands]")` is a slot — but the spec (PRIMITIVES.md:747) says the collapse is signalled specifically by *"the removal of a candidate."* `closest` also matches the slot itself, so a `REMOVE_CHILD` whose parent is the slot for **any other reason** (e.g. a same-component fit swap that morphs `controls → compactControls` and removes the `volumeView` + a divider, `Emitter.reconcileNode`→`reconcileChildren`) unwraps the gate while the loser candidates remain. On the rotate, that's exactly when a band crossing forces such a swap.
2. **App tree ↔ client DOM divergence across a reconnect.** iOS suspends the tab on rotate → WS drops → reconnect → `META::RESYNC`. `renderFull()` replays the *retained* tree. If the app's tree is the snapshot form but the client already tore its gate down (or vice-versa), the replay's `CREATE`/`INSERT` are skipped (`apply.ts:508-514`) and nothing restores the gate → losers stay visible.
3. **Nested slots.** The demo has two nested fit slots (root row `0/1024`, bar controls `0/700`), and *both* outer candidates embed a copy of the bar's inner slot. A stray removal under one slot can tear the wrong gate.
4. **WebKit `@container` re-evaluation on orientation change** (less likely — a stale query would still show *one* candidate, not all, so this alone can't explain "all branches").

No stale-bundle cause: the deployed demo bundle matches `dist` exactly (`sha256 d903f2af059d`).

## How I'd debug it

**On the iPhone (Safari Web Inspector via a Mac):** reproduce the rotate, then inspect the slot(s):
- Does the slot still have `data-pathland-fit-cands` + `container-name:pf-<id>`? Are the `data-pathland-fit-cand` wrappers still there? Is `style[data-pathland-fit]` present with the `@container` rules?
  - wrappers present + rules present + all visible → **CSS/`@container` bug**.
  - wrappers gone / `container-name` stripped → **the gate was torn down** (hypothesis 1/2).
- Check the console with `?pathland-log=debug` (`src/log.ts`) — the client logs every `← recv frame`/opcode; look for the `REMOVE_CHILD`/`DELETE_NODE` that coincides with the break, and whether it targets a *candidate*.

**Locally (deterministic):** the gaps that let this through are that `sizethatfits-snapshot`/`-three` are **not** in the SSR-conformance list (`ssr-conformance.test.ts:17`) and there's no test for the *rotate sequence*. A repro harness in `fit.test.ts` should: hydrate the snapshot fixture → apply the app's N→1 downgrade → apply a band-crossing fit swap (morph with a child removal) → apply a `META::RESYNC` → assert **exactly one** visible candidate.

## Proposed fixes (to confirm/decide with you)

- **A — Narrow the teardown to the real downgrade:** in `collapseFitSlotFor`, only collapse when the removed/deleted node is actually a candidate (its id matches a `data-pathland-fit-cand-id` in the slot), per the spec — instead of any structural removal.
- **B — Make it atomic / self-healing:** collapse in a *post-batch* step only when the slot has ended with a single child (i.e. tear down the gate *after* the `REMOVE`/`DELETE` deltas are applied), so an unrelated removal can never leave the losers exposed.
- **C — JS visibility fallback:** have `evaluateFit` also toggle the candidate `display` in the snapshot form, so first-paint gating no longer depends solely on `@container` re-evaluation.
- **D — Tests + spec sync:** add the snapshot fixtures to `ssr-conformance`, add the rotate-sequence regression test, and update the affected `status.md`.

## Root cause (the core issue)

The SSR first paint is gated **only by CSS** (wrappers + `@container` band rules). That gate is torn down by an **eager, over-broad, non-atomic** rule in the DOM client:

- `apply.ts:456` fires `collapseFitSlotFor` on **any** `REMOVE_CHILD`/`DELETE_NODE` whose nearest `[data-pathland-fit-cands]` ancestor (via `closest`, which also matches the slot itself) is a still-gated slot — the spec (`PRIMITIVES.md:747`) says the collapse is signalled specifically by **"the removal of a candidate."**
- `collapseFitSlotFor` (`apply.ts:1434-1459`) **unwraps every `data-pathland-fit-cand` wrapper, strips the container, and drops the band rules immediately** — before knowing whether the app's deltas actually remove the losers.

So if *any* structural removal happens under a slot that hasn't yet been downgraded, the gate is destroyed but the loser candidates remain as plain visible children → **all branches rendered**. This is permanent until a later same-component swap morphs the slot back to one child.

A **rotate** is exactly when this fires: the width crosses a fit band, the app swaps the slot's child, and the swap emits `REMOVE_CHILD`s under the slot — e.g. the bar's `controls → compactControls` removes the volume slider + a divider, and the root row's `wideRow → compactRow` removes the sidebar. Deterministic on iOS (a rotate always crosses a band in that order); intermittent on desktop (only when a resize crosses a band with that op ordering).

- New test: a gated slot with 2 candidates; apply a `REMOVE_CHILD`/`DELETE_NODE` targeting a **non-candidate** node inside a candidate → assert the gate **survives** (wrappers + `container-name` + band rules intact, one candidate visible). This fails today.

- In `applyBatch`, after the op loop (right before `applyLayout`, `apply.ts:373`), run `reconcileFitGate(slot)` per recorded slot:
  - count the slot's **live** candidates (wrappers that still contain an element child);

Fixes the intermittent **"all branches rendered"** bug (SizeThatFits candidates all visible) after the app has been hydrated — reliably reproducible on iOS rotate (landscape → portrait), intermittently on a desktop resize.

## Cause
The DOM client tore the SSR SizeThatFits gate down on **any** `REMOVE_CHILD`/`DELETE_NODE` under a `data-pathland-fit-cands` slot (`apply.ts`), eagerly unwrapping every `data-pathland-fit-cand` wrapper **before** knowing whether the deltas actually removed the losers. A band-crossing fit swap that drops a child **inside** a candidate — e.g. the player bar's wide→compact swap removing the volume slider + a divider — therefore unwrapped the gate but left the loser candidates in place → every candidate visible. A rotate always crosses a fit band, so it hits this reliably.

## Fix
Reconcile the gate **after** the batch (`reconcileFitGate`), gated on the slot's **final** state: only a slot that ended with a **single live candidate** (the app's N→1 downgrade) is unwrapped (survivor lifted out, empty wrappers dropped, `container-name`/cands + band rules stripped). A removal that leaves **more than one** live candidate leaves the gate intact (the CSS band keeps showing one). An `INSERT_CHILD`/`CREATE_NODE` (a `META::RESYNC` replay) still never collapses it — this matches the spec's "signalled by the removal of a candidate".

## Verified
- New regression: a **non-candidate** removal under a gated slot keeps the gate (fails before, passes after).
- New `ssr-conformance` case: hydrate the real `sizethatfits-snapshot` fixture + apply the N→1 downgrade → the gate collapses to the plain single-child form.
- `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 236 pass; existing fit tests (incl. the resync-keeps-the-gate case) still green.
- DOM bundle rebuilt into both demos (`d903f2af059d` → `a14cb2a355ee`).
EOF

# Pathland server runtime — architecture research

Scope explored:
- `lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/` (all classes)
- `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-starter/` and `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/` (all main classes)
- Supporting `pathland-view` contracts: `transport/FrameCodec`, `emit/*`, `state/*`, `signal/Signals`, `Platform`, `Environment`
- The DOM client `lib/typescript/src/{index,transport,plpl}.ts` and the Rust SSR renderer `pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs`
- Dependency manifests (`pom.xml`, `Cargo.toml`)

---

## 1. Root view, session creation, lifecycle, threads, per-session state

### `PathlandApp` — the app-specific factory
`PathlandApp.java:15-25` is a functional interface; the *only* app-specific piece the runtime needs:

```java
@FunctionalInterface
public interface PathlandApp {
    View newRoot();                          // line 19 — a FRESH root view per session
    default ThemeData theme() { return null; } // line 22
}
```

`PathlandSession` calls `app.newRoot()` on mount (line 138), so every session gets its own view instance and therefore its own `State` fields.

### `PathlandSession` — one app instance per client
`PathlandSession.java:38-243`. Javadoc (lines 23-37): "One Pathland application instance per session (1:1 with a client). Owns the session's PersistentState, the retained tree, the fine-grained emitter, and the single connection it sends deltas to."

Key constructor (the full one), `PathlandSession.java:89-143`:

```java
public PathlandSession(String sessionId, StateStore store, PathlandApp app, EnvironmentData env,
                       boolean debugHtml, String base, String stateScope,
                       PathlandTelemetry telemetry, String mount) {
    ...
    this.state = new PersistentState(store, stateScope);          // :103  per-session state scope
    this.activePath = Signals.signal(env.route());                // :106  Platform.ACTIVE_PATH seed
    this.sink = new FrameOpcodeSink() {                           // :108-125
        @Override public void endFrame() {
            super.endFrame();
            PathlandConnection conn = connection;
            if (conn == null || !conn.isOpen()) return;           // mount frame is NEVER sent
            ProtocolFrame frame = frame();
            if (!frame.opcodes().isEmpty()) batcher.append(frame);
        }
    };
    this.batcher = new DeltaBatcher(this::sendBatch, this.telemetry, this.mount); // :126
    this.emitter = new Emitter(sink, app.theme());                // :127
    this.emitter.snapshotEmission(true);                          // :132
    RenderResult result = emitter.mount(                          // :137-139
        app.newRoot().modifiers(environmentBinding(
            e -> e.key(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH).value(activePath))),
        new Environment(state));
    this.inputDispatcher = new InputDispatcher(result, activePath); // :140
    this.rootId = result.rootId();                                  // :141
    applyEnvironment(env);                                          // :142
}
```

Lifecycle / thread model:
- **Threads**: state wiring/mount happens on the **constructing thread**. For a live session that is the registry's **single actor thread** (`PathlandRegistry` line 53-57, thread named `pathland-actor`); for SSR it is the **request thread** with a throwaway session (see §4). Signals are single-threaded by contract, and all session work is serialized on the actor.
- **Connection is wired after mount**: `connect(PathlandConnection)` (line 157-159). The comment at lines 112-115 explains why: "Only live deltas go out: the mount frame (emitted in the constructor, before the session attaches) is NOT sent — the client already has the whole UI from the HTML."
- **Per-session state scope**: `new PersistentState(store, stateScope)`; `stateScope` is the app-qualified per-window id supplied by the registry. `Environment(state)` is passed to `mount`, and `Environment.state()` returns it (`Environment.java:84`) — this is how views auto-connect `State` fields (see §5).
- `applyEnvironment(EnvironmentData)` (146-154) re-sets `activePath` (re-route, guard-aware) and records viewport.
- `resync()` (162-165): `emitter.renderFull(); batcher.flush();` — a full snapshot (META::RESYNC response).
- `sendBatch(byte[])` (173-186): drops the connection on failure (`connection = null; closeConnection(conn)`), so the client reconnects.
- `dispatch(byte[])` / `dispatch(Iterable<Event>)` (200-211): routes inbound raw events into `inputDispatcher`.
- `renderHtml()` (214-234): SSR only (see §2).
- `close()` (237-242): `state.close(); emitter.destroy(); batcher.close(); connection = null;`.

**Emission is diff-based** via `Emitter` (`emit/Emitter.java`): `mount` (99-152) assigns pre-order ids and emits the structural frame; `registerBindings` (333) registers one node-level effect per reactive text/property so a signal change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` (zero opcodes when unchanged). `renderFull` (164-179) replays the retained tree. The **single root id** is `emitter.rootId()`; there is exactly one retained tree and one `FrameOpcodeSink` per session.

## 2. `PathlandConnection`, SSR HTML, and the `/ws` endpoints

### 2a. `PathlandConnection` — the outbound seam
`PathlandConnection.java:8-15`:

```java
public interface PathlandConnection {
    void send(byte[] bytes);   // a self-contained PLPL delta/snapshot batch
    boolean isOpen();
}
```

The session only ever calls `send(bytes)`/`isOpen()`. Both starters adapt their framework socket to it.

### 2b. SSR HTML path
`PathlandSession.renderHtml()` (214-234):

```java
HtmlRenderer renderer = HtmlRenderer.tryInstance();
String html = debugHtml ? renderer.renderDebug(sink.frame(), rootId)
                        : renderer.render(sink.frame(), rootId);
return html
  .replace("<html>", "<html data-pathland-base=\"" + base + "\">")
  .replace("</body>", "<script src=\"" + base + "/" + PathlandAssets.bundleName()
          + "\" defer></script></body>");
```

- The HTML is produced by the **Rust renderer** (`HtmlRenderer.render` → C ABI `pathland_html_render`, `HtmlRenderer.java:227-309`). `render_document` in `pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs:1173-1205` emits:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Pathland</title>
{builtin CSS}{<style data-pathland-tokens>…}{<style data-pathland-fit>…}
</head><body>{tree}</body></html>
```

  Every node carries a stable id: `data-pathland-id="{id}"` (`lib.rs:1231`), plus `data-event-listeners="{mask}"` (`lib.rs:789`), `data-pathland-media`, `data-pathland-fit`/`-cands`, `data-pathland-depth`, etc.

- **No `<html>`/`</head>` rewriting beyond that; no state is embedded in the HTML** — the client hydrates from the SSR DOM and then re-syncs state over WS.

**Hydration (client)** — `lib/typescript/src/index.ts`:
- `boot()` (103) builds `byId: Map<number, Node>` from `document.querySelectorAll("[data-pathland-id]")` (105-107).
- Reads `document.documentElement.dataset.pathlandBase` (112) → derives the mount prefix (118-119) and the WS URL `${base}/ws?wid=${wid}` (146).

- On socket open `onOpen` (151-168): sends `META::ENVIRONMENT` (viewport + `location.pathname`) as the first message; refreshes fit slots; and if `isReload || urlHadWid` sends `encodeResync()`.
- Deltas are applied in place by `applyBatch` (from `apply.ts`); routing by `data-pathland-id` + `data-event-listeners` mask (helpers `nodeOf`/`eventNodeOf`/`listens`, lines 46-88).

- `pathlandWebSocketConfigurer` (119-124) registers **one handler per mounted app**:

```

---

## 3. What flows over `/ws`

### Wire format — PLPL, self-contained
`FrameCodec.java:13-40` and the identical TS `plpl.ts:34-77`:

```
magic "PLPL" (u32 LE) | version (u16) | flags (u16) | sequence (u32)
| opcodeCount (u32) | opcodes (16B × count) | stringsLen (u32) | string bytes
```

Constants: `MAGIC=0x504C504C`, `VERSION=1`, `GUEST_TO_HOST=0x0000`, `HOST_TO_GUEST=0x0001`, `HEADER=16` (`FrameCodec.java:34-38`). Every batch is a **single WebSocket binary message** (test-kit comment `WsSession.java:27-29`) and is self-contained (relative string offsets — `ProtocolFrame`).

Both directions share the header; direction is the `flags` bit.

### guest → host (client → server) message kinds
Handled in the socket `onBinary` (Quarkus `PathlandSocket.java:84-110` / Spring `PathlandSocket.java:53-80`):
1. `META::ENVIRONMENT` (`FrameCodec.encodeEnvironment`, 106-129; fields ROUTE + viewport) — the **first** message; seeds/creates the session.
2. `META::RESYNC` (`encodeResync`, 79-85) — asks for a full snapshot.
3. `META::PING` (`encodePing`, 97-103) — transport heartbeat; server replies `META::PONG` (`encodePong`, 88-94) **at the transport layer**, no actor/session touch.
4. Otherwise an **event batch**: `FrameCodec.encodeEvents` / `decodeEvents` (188-292) — `EVENT`-category opcodes (POINTER_DOWN/MOVE/UP, KEY_DOWN/UP, TEXT_CHANGED, VALUE_CHANGED, EDITING_CHANGED, FOCUS_CHANGED, DATE_CHANGED, SUBMIT, NAVIGATE, SCROLL/WHEEL, MEDIA_*, FIT_CHANGED).

META command ids: `ENVIRONMENT=0x02, RESYNC=0x03, PING=0x04, PONG=0x05` (`Commands.java:61-67`).

### host → client (server → client)
- **Deltas**: per-signal frames from the `Emitter`, coalesced by `DeltaBatcher` and encoded with `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, sequence)` (`DeltaBatcher.java:124-138`). The per-session **monotonic `sequence`** (`nextSequence`, 55; `flush`, 134) enables client gap detection.
- **Full snapshot** for RESYNC: `Emitter.renderFull()` (164-179) → `batcher.flush()`.
- `PONG` (transport-level) and the HTML bundle/asset responses.

### META::RESYNC (client) → full snapshot (server)
Registry path: `resync(sessionId)` (`PathlandRegistry.java:201-206`) → actor → `session.resync()` → `emitter.renderFull()`. Client requests it on reconnect (`transport.ts:163-166`), same-tab reload (`index.ts:164-167`), a `wid` carried on the SSR URL (164), and on a **sequence gap** (`transport.ts:229-237`).

### Per-window id selection
The `wid` does **not** select a session — it selects the **persisted-state scope**. Session identity is the fresh per-connection `uiId` (`registry.open(uiId, windowId, connection)`, `PathlandRegistry.java:165-173`; the `windowId` is stored as `PendingSession.stateScope`, line 276). See §4/§5. Two windows of one browser never share a session even with the same `wid` (status.md:107-108).

### Events → state signals
`PathlandSession.dispatch` (200-211) → `InputDispatcher.dispatch` (`InputDispatcher.java:45-123`). The dispatcher looks up, by `event.target()` node id, one of the routing maps from `RenderResult`:
- pointer-up → `navigateActions` (nav intent wins) else `tapActions`;
- TEXT_CHANGED → `textInputs`; VALUE_CHANGED → `valueInputs`; EDITING/FOCUS → `editingInputs`; DATE → `dateInputs`; MEDIA_* → `mediaInputs`; FIT_CHANGED → `fitInputs`; NAVIGATE URL → writes `activePath` (the `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal), else the global `navigateHandler`.

Those consumers are wired by views to signals. E.g. `TextField.java:72-76`:

```java
node.textBinding = config.binding;   // WritableSignal<String>
node.text = config.binding.get();
node.textInput = config.binding::set; // TEXT_CHANGED writes the signal
```

`Slider.java:73`: `node.valueInput = config.binding::set;`. The signal write synchronously runs the emitter's node-level effect (`Emitter.registerNodeBindings`, 360-406), which emits that node's delta. `RenderResult`'s maps are live views, so structural reconciles update routing after mount (`RenderResult.java:8-15`).

Client heartbeat/watchdog and sequence handling live in `transport.ts` (constants 46-48; `startHeartbeat` 111-129; `handleMessage` 194-249; `isSequenceGap` 256-261; version mismatch reload 219-223).

---

## 4. `PathlandRegistry` — lifecycle, 1:1 mapping, actor thread

`PathlandRegistry.java:41-278`. One registry **per mounted app** (own actor + maps + base + state scope).

- **Actor thread** (53-57): a single daemon thread `pathland-actor` via `Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor`. Javadoc 37-39: "All session work is serialized on a single actor thread (signals are single-threaded by contract). Per-session SSR runs on the request thread against the thread-safe StateStore (a throwaway PathlandSession)."
- **Maps** (59-60): `ConcurrentHashMap<String, PathlandSession> sessions` and `ConcurrentHashMap<String, PendingSession> pending`.
- **1:1 mapping**: keyed by `uiId` (a fresh per-connection id). `open(uiId, windowId, conn)` (165-173) removes any previous session with the same `uiId` and stores a `PendingSession(stateScope(windowId), connection)`.
- **Lazy session creation on first inbound message**: `open` only registers the pending connection. `environment(sessionId, env)` (176-179) → `session(sessionId, appEnv).applyEnvironment(...)`. `session(...)` (237-251) creates the `PathlandSession` on first contact, wires the pending connection after mount, and puts it in `sessions`.
- **Operations**: `environment` (176), `dispatch` (182-198, with `MAX_EVENT_BATCH = 1<<16` guard), `resync` (201-206), `close(sessionId)` (209-218), `shutdown()` (221-229, closes all + shuts the actor), `activeSessions()` (232-234).
- **SSR** (request thread): `renderHtml(route, windowId)` (137-152) creates a **throwaway** `PathlandSession`, renders, and `session.close()`s it. `windowId` normally absent → defaults; the client re-syncs.
- Route/mount helpers: `mountPath()` (89), `base()` (94-96), `stateScope(windowId)` (103-105), `stripRoute(route)` (112-126), `stripNavigateUrls` (264-273).

`PendingSession` record: `record PendingSession(String stateScope, PathlandConnection connection)` (276).

Related: `PathlandHost` (`PathlandHost.java:24-129`) hosts N `MountedApp`s (`MountedApp.java:18`), each with its own registry; `match(requestUri)` (75-86) does longest-prefix dispatch and returns `MountMatch(registry, route)` (127).

---

## 5. `StateStores` — the contract

`StateStore.java:15-25` — the platform-neutral contract:

```java
public interface StateStore {
    <T> Optional<T> load(String key, Class<T> clazz);
    void save(String key, Object state);
    void delete(String key);
}
```

Untyped (one store for all signal types).

- **In-memory**: `InMemoryStateStore.java:12-39` — `ConcurrentHashMap`; thread-safe so a request thread can read while the session actor writes.
- **Redis**: `dev.pathland.state.redis.RedisStateStore` (in `pathland-state-redis`) via `RedisStateStore.Provider().store()`.
- **Default selection**: `StateStores.redisOrFallback(StateStore fallback)` (`StateStores.java:20-30`) — probes Redis (`load("probe", Object.class)`), else fallback. Quarkus binds it in `PathlandRegistryProducer.host` (98); Spring binds it in `pathlandStateStore()` (`PathlandAutoConfiguration.java:57-61`), both `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`-overridable.
- **Consumer**: `PersistentState` (`PersistentState.java:35-62`) — `signal(name, initial)` loads `key = name + ":" + scope` and auto-saves on change (`Signals.effect(... store.save(key, signal.get()))`). `connect(view)` (73-96) reflectively invokes the generated `<View>_StateBinder` to wire `State` fields. `Environment.state()` returns this per-session handle.

---

## 6. Where an outbound HTTP/WS client could go (server-to-server)

### Does the codebase already have an HTTP/WS client? Almost none.
- **No REST/WS client dependency in any Java `pom.xml`**: the only client is the **JDK** `java.net.http.HttpClient` + `java.net.http.WebSocket`, used in `pathland-test-kit` (main scope) and a couple of tests:
  - `lib/java/pathland-test-kit/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/test/WsSession.java:10-11,34` — `private static final HttpClient HTTP = HttpClient.newHttpClient();` and `HTTP.newWebSocketBuilder().buildAsync(URI.create(wsBaseUrl + "?wid=" + wid), listener)` (88-94). It speaks the full PLPL protocol (environment/resync/click/ping) and decodes batches with `FrameCodec.decodeFrame` (55).
- **Quarkus starter** deps: `quarkus-rest`, `quarkus-websockets-next`, `quarkus-micrometer`, `quarkus-smallrye-health` (`pathland-quarkus-starter/pom.xml:35-48`). No `quarkus-rest-client` / `quarkus-websockets-client`.
- **Spring starter** deps: `spring-boot-starter-web`, `-websocket`, `-actuator` (`pathland-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml:35-44`). No WebClient/WebFlux/OkHttp.
- **Rust** has no HTTP/WS client (`Cargo.toml` files and `Cargo.lock` show no `reqwest`/`tungstenite`/`hyper`/`ureq`).

So the *only* existing outbound-capable code is the test-kit `WsSession`.

### Where it architecturally belongs
The outbound server-to-server link is the **mirror image of `PathlandConnection`**:
- **Server → client** today: `PathlandConnection.send(byte[])` / `isOpen()` (the seam implemented by `QuarkusConnection`/`SpringConnection`).
- **Server → other server** would need a new seam on the **host** side: something like `PathlandRemoteConnection` that both (a) **receives** B's PLPL batches (B's deltas/snapshot) and (b) **sends** event batches to B — exactly what `pathland-test-kit.WsSession` already demonstrates client-side.

Concretely, the natural insertion points:
1. A new server-core abstraction (e.g. `PathlandProxy` / `RemoteSession`) that owns one outbound connection to B and translates B's opcode stream into A's tree. It would use `FrameCodec` for decode/encode (`decodeFrame`, `decodeEvents`, `encodeEvents`, `encodeEnvironment`, `encodeResync`), all already in `pathland-view`, so no new wire code is required.
2. A **client transport** per starter:
   - Quarkus: `quarkus-websockets-client` (a `@WebSocketClient` / `WebSocketConnector`) or a `quarkus-rest-client`-reactive call for SSR of B's HTML.
   - Spring: `StandardWebSocketClient` (`spring-websocket`, already on the classpath) or `WebClient` (`spring-webflux`).
   - Or, framework-free, the JDK `HttpClient`/`WebSocket` as in `WsSession`.
3. The `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry` wiring in each starter is where such a bean would be produced (`pathland-quarkus-starter/.../PathlandRegistryProducer.java:89-99`, `pathland-spring-boot-starter/.../PathlandAutoConfiguration.java:98-113`).

### The hard architectural constraint for a "proxy view"
The emitter/SSR model is **single-root and single-id-space**:
- `Emitter` assigns ids from **one counter** `nextId` starting at 1 (`Emitter.java:119-120, 197-202, 566-568`) and yields **one `rootId`** (140-141). A `FrameOpcodeSink` holds one frame.
- SSR renders exactly one root: `HtmlRenderer.render(frame, rootId)` → Rust `render_document(..., root)` (`pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs:1173`).
- The session's emitter is the **sole producer**; nothing in `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` consumes foreign opcodes, and `InputDispatcher` routes strictly by A-assigned node id (`InputDispatcher.java:52-123`).

Therefore embedding B's subtree inside A means **splicing** B's nodes into A's retained tree, not nesting a second tree: B's opcodes must be **rebased into A's id space** (offset/remap `A`/`B`/`C` node-id fields and the `TREE` commands), and B's events must be **routed from the proxy node back out** to B. The existing `PathlandNode.structuralContent` slot (`PathlandNode.java:126`) + `Emitter.reconcileSlot` (`Emitter.java:428-531`) is the nearest analog for a dynamically-mounted subtree (it diffs a retained child subtree into `TREE` deltas), but it renders from a `View`, not from a foreign opcode stream — so a proxy node would need a new emitter sink path (or a new "foreign subtree" concept in the engine/spec). No such component exists (see §7).

---

## 7. Multiple roots / multiple sessions per connection / multiplexing

- **Multiple root views**: yes, but at the **server-process level**, not per connection. `MountedApp(path, app)` (`MountedApp.java:18`) + `PathlandHost` (`PathlandHost.java:24-129`) host any number of apps, each with its **own `PathlandRegistry`, own actor thread, own `base()` (`/<mount>/_pathland`), own state scope, and own `/ws` endpoint**. `match(requestUri)` picks the longest mount prefix. In Quarkus the lone `PathlandApp` mounts at `/` unless a `MountedApp` claims it (`PathlandRegistryProducer.java:93-98`); Spring identical (`PathlandAutoConfiguration.java:106-112`). Web endpoints per app: Quarkus `PathlandSocket` (root) + `MountedPathlandSocket` (one path segment `/{app}`) (status.md:99-101), Spring one `PathlandSocket` per registry.
- **Multiple sessions per connection**: **none.** Every connection = exactly one `uiId` = one `PathlandSession` = one retained tree. `PathlandRegistry` docs (lines 19-22): "1:1 sessions keyed by a per-connection id… two windows of the same browser never share a session."
- **Multiplexing**: **none.** There is no channel/frame-id field; the PLPL header carries only `flags` + a per-stream `sequence`. The only coalescing is `DeltaBatcher` merging many frames into one batch (`DeltaBatcher.java:90-139`). There is **no notion of multiple roots on one connection**, no sub-session ids, and no event routing by anything other than the A-assigned node id (`InputDispatcher`). `PathlandSession` has a single `connection` field (63) and a single `rootId` (55).

### Spec check
There is **no** "proxy/remote/embed/foreign/iframe/host-view" primitive or command in the specs (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/OPCODE.md`, `spec/DSL.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md` — greps for `proxy|remote|embed|iframe|multiplex` found only prose about HTTP proxies and "embedded displays"/"embedded bundle"). The only closeness is the "reserved framework root `/_pathland/**`… a host can relocate it behind a proxy" (`spec/DSL.md:604-607`) — unrelated to view proxying.

---

## Summary implications for a "proxy view" feature

1. **Session model is 1:1 and single-root** — a proxy node cannot be a nested second tree shipped as-is; it must be merged into A's single retained tree. That requires **id-space rebasing** (`Emitter.nextId` is one global counter) and a way to mark a subtree as foreign (for event routing back to B).
2. **The wire is already language/platform neutral and symmetric** (`FrameCodec`, PLPL, host↔guest EVENT batches). A server acting as a client to B is fully expressible with existing codecs — the test-kit `WsSession` is a working reference.
3. **The outbound seam does not exist yet**; the cleanest insertion is a new server-core `RemoteSession`/`PathlandProxy` abstraction plus a starter-provided client transport (Quarkus websockets-client/rest-client, Spring `StandardWebSocketClient`/`WebClient`, or JDK `HttpClient` as in `WsSession`). No HTTP/WS client dependency is currently declared.
4. **Events**: a proxy node's raw events (targeted at B's nodes) must be forwarded to B via `FrameCodec.encodeEvents`; A's `InputDispatcher` currently drops events for unknown ids, so the proxy needs a catch-all/prefix route.
5. **SSR**: `HtmlRenderer.render` renders one `root`; embedding B's SSR subtree in A's first paint would require composing the two rendered fragments (B has its own `data-pathland-id` space), or omitting B from SSR and hydrating it over WS.

Key files to revisit when implementing: `PathlandSession.java`, `PathlandRegistry.java`, `PathlandHost.java`, `pathland-view/.../emit/Emitter.java`, `emit/PathlandNode.java`, `transport/FrameCodec.java`, and both starters' socket/config classes.

# Pathland DOM Renderer (lib/typescript) — current client behavior

**Bottom line up front:** today's client is a **document-global singleton**. It hydrates *every* `[data-pathland-id]` in the page into one flat `Map<number, Node>`, opens exactly **one** WebSocket, and applies one opcode stream. There is **no** notion of a root container, no id namespacing, no second connection, and no per-stream scoping. A "proxy view" that interleaves a second server's subtree into one DOM will collide on all of these. Details below.

Everything is bundled by esbuild into `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` as an **IIFE** (`package.json:9`), and `src/index.ts` **auto-boots as a module side effect** — there is no exported factory to instantiate a second renderer.

---

## 1. SSR hydration

**Entry point / hydration:** `boot()` in `src/index.ts:103`, invoked either on `DOMContentLoaded` or immediately if the document is already parsed:

```ts
// src/index.ts:519-523
if (document.readyState === "loading") {
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", boot);
} else {
  boot();
}
```

**The `data-pathland-id` → DOM map** is built by scanning the *entire document* into one flat numeric map (`src/index.ts:104-107`):

```ts
const byId = new Map<number, Node>();
for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("[data-pathland-id]")) {
  byId.set(Number(el.getAttribute("data-pathland-id")), el);
}
```

**The shape it expects** — `DomRenderer` (`src/apply.ts:310-337`):

```ts
export interface DomRenderer {
  byId: Map<number, Node>;
  onRoute?: (path: string) => void;
  onNavigateBack?: () => void;
  tokenSink?: DesignTokenSink;
  onMediaEvent?: (batch: Uint8Array) => void;
  onFitEvent?: (batch: Uint8Array) => void;
}
```

No root pointer is stored: the registry is flat and the numeric key is the sole address. The tree's root is by **convention id `1`** (all golden fixtures and tests use `data-pathland-id="1"` as the root, e.g. `test/fixtures/ssr/counter.html:1`, and `renderFresh(bytes, 1)` in `test/ssr-conformance.test.ts:158-162`). Nothing in the client enforces or discovers that.

After building the map, `boot()` additionally hydrates side-car attributes:
- media nodes: `[data-pathland-media]` → `setupMediaElement` (`index.ts:188-190`)
- fit slots: `[data-pathland-fit]` → `hydrateFitElement` (`index.ts:200-202`)
- nav back buttons: `updateNavBackButtons` (`index.ts:233`)
- reserved framework base from `document.documentElement.dataset.pathlandBase` (`index.ts:112`; also read in `icons.ts:19-21`)

The test harness mirrors this hydration (`test/ssr-conformance.test.ts:165-173`):

```ts
function hydrate(fragment: string): DomRenderer {
  const host = document.createElement("div");
  host.innerHTML = fragment;
  const byId = new Map<number, Node>();
  for (const el of host.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("[data-pathland-id]")) {
    byId.set(Number(el.getAttribute("data-pathland-id")), el);
  }
  return { byId };
}
```

Core element lookup casts the attribute to a number on every access, e.g. `Number(node.getAttribute("data-pathland-id"))` (`index.ts:253, 305, 332, 388`).

---

## 2. PLPL batch decode

**Decode entry point:** `parseBatch(bytes: Uint8Array): Batch` (`src/plpl.ts:34`). Called from `Transport.handleMessage` (`src/transport.ts:209`).

**Batch shape** (`src/plpl.ts:12-19`, `3-10`):

```ts
export interface Opcode { category: number; command: number; flags: number; a: number; b: number; c: number; }
export interface Batch {
  readonly version: number;
  readonly flags: number;
  readonly sequence: number;
  readonly opcodes: Opcode[];
  readonly strings: Uint8Array;
}
```

**Wire layout** (documented at `src/plpl.ts:28-33`, constants in `src/constants.ts:5-10`): a self-contained batch is

```
[magic u32=0x504c504c][version u16=1][flags u16][sequence u32][opcodeCount u32]   // 16-byte header
opcodeCount × 16-byte opcodes                                                     // category|command|flags|A|B|C
[stringsLen u32][strings…]                                                        // the "string arena" section
```

Parsing is fully bounds-checked and throws `ProtocolError` (`plpl.ts:22`) on truncation/bad magic/version (`plpl.ts:35-69`). Each opcode is read little-endian at `HEADER_SIZE + i*16` (`plpl.ts:54-64`).

**Sections:** there are exactly three — header, opcodes, and a single trailing `strings` byte blob. There is **no separate events or multiple-string section** in the batch; a batch is homogeneous. The `strings` blob holds variable-length entries that opcodes reference by *relative u32 offset*:

- `readString(strings, offset): string` — `[u32 len][utf8…]` (`plpl.ts:80-91`)
- `readList(strings, offset): number[]` — `[u32 count][f32 × count]`, used for `FIT_QUERY` (`plpl.ts:96-111`)

Events use the *same* batch envelope but carry `CAT_EVENT` opcodes and flags `0x0000` (guest→host); e.g. `eventBatch()` (`src/events.ts:41-57`). Text events put the payload in the string section (`encodeTextChanged`, `events.ts:170-191`).

---

## 3. Delta application

**Entry point:** `applyBatch(batch: Batch, renderer: DomRenderer): void` (`src/apply.ts:340`). It switches on `op.category` (`apply.ts:348-363`):

```ts
case CAT_TREE:      applyTree(op, renderer, touchedFitGates); break;
case CAT_PARAMETER: applyStyle(op, batch.strings, renderer); break;
case CAT_META:      applyMeta(op, renderer); break;
```

After the loop it reconciles touched fit-gates and runs `applyLayout(renderer)` (whole-tree derived layout, `apply.ts:378-384`).

### The id → element map and parent tracking

- **`byId: Map<number, Node>`** is the only registry (`apply.ts:311`). It is flat and keyed by the raw protocol node id.
- **Component type per node** is tracked in a separate `WeakMap` (`apply.ts:100`): `const componentByNode = new WeakMap<Node, number>();` — needed because hydrated SSR nodes have no component recorded.
- **Parents are NOT tracked as protocol state.** Parent/child relationships are derived from the actual DOM via `Node.parentElement` when needed:
  - layout: `const parent = el.parentElement` (`apply.ts:290`)
  - fit-gate collapse: `treeOpParent(op, r)` resolves the parent from `byId` + DOM (`apply.ts:1424-1435`)
- The **container an op inserts into** is `childrenContainer(parent)` (`src/elements.ts:315-328`), which routes children into composite sub-nodes (menu-items, toggle text span, textfield label span) and otherwise returns the node itself.

### TREE commands — `applyTree(op, r, touchedFitGates)` (`apply.ts:455`)

- **`CMD_CREATE_NODE`** (`apply.ts:474-490`): **hydration-aware** — if `op.a` already exists in `byId` it *reuses* the hydrated element; only when absent does it call `createElement(op.b)` (`elements.ts:42`) and set `data-pathland-id`. `op.a = node id`, `op.b = component type`.

- **`CMD_INSERT_CHILD`** (`apply.ts:506-543`): `op.a = parent id`, `op.b = child id`, `op.c = index`. - **`CMD_REMOVE_CHILD`** (`apply.ts:544-550`): `op.b` child, removes from its `parentNode` (does **not** delete the registry entry).
- **`CMD_MOVE_CHILD`** (`apply.ts:551-585`): `op.a = new parent`, `op.b = child`, `op.c = index`.
- **`insertAt(container, child, index)`** (`apply.ts:591-619`): index counts **element children only**, excluding the injected `.pathland-nav-back` button (`NAV_BACK_CLASS`, `apply.ts:628`); skips inserting a node into its own subtree; `detachIfWrongParent` first.
- **`placedChild(parent, child)`** (`apply.ts:410-429`): ZStack/grid children get wrapped in a shell `<div>` before insertion.

### PARAMETER commands — `applyStyle(op, strings, r)` (`apply.ts:806`)

- `CMD_SET_TEXT` (`apply.ts:817`), `CMD_SET_DATE` (`apply.ts:820`), `CMD_SET_PROPERTY` (`apply.ts:837`), `CMD_SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (`apply.ts:807` → `applyDesignToken`, `tokens.ts:105`).
- `SET_PROPERTY` decodes `propId = op.b & 0xffff` and `valueType = (op.b >>> 16) & 0xff`; STRING values are read from the string section at offset `op.c`; special-cased properties (ROLE, TEXT_STYLE, NAV_DEPTH, NAV_CHROME, PROGRESS, media, etc.) are dispatched in `applyStringProperty` (`apply.ts:952`) and `applyNumericProperty` (`apply.ts:1047`).

### Root / container identification

There is **no root identification** in the client. A node becomes "the root" purely because it is the top of the DOM and is referenced by convention as id 1. There is no `data-pathland-root` attribute anywhere in the repo (searched). `META::RESET` (`applyMeta`, `apply.ts:386-401`) iterates **every** `byId` value and removes it, then `r.byId.clear()` — i.e. reset is *global*, not scoped.

### Node-id scope

**Global numeric namespace, shared by the entire document.** Ids are never namespaced, prefixed, or qualified by connection/stream. Two streams that both use id 1, 2, 3… will overwrite each other in `byId`.

---

## 4. Event sending

Event capture is a set of **document-level listeners** registered in `boot()`:

- pointerdown / pointermove / pointerout / click (`index.ts:248-353`)
- keydown / keyup (`index.ts:356-373`)
- focusin / focusout (`index.ts:383-408`)
- scroll / wheel (`index.ts:411-432`)
- change (toggle/select/color/date) (`index.ts:435-484`)
- input (slider/textfield/editor) (`index.ts:487-516`)

**How a node id is attached:** the event target is resolved to its nearest `[data-pathland-id]` ancestor, then `Number(...)` is passed as the event's target `A` field.

Two resolvers:
- `nodeOf(el): HTMLElement | null` — deepest `[data-pathland-id]` via `closest` (`index.ts:46-48`)
- `eventNodeOf(target, bit): HTMLElement | null` — walks up until it finds a node whose `data-event-listeners` mask includes `bit` (`index.ts:60-72`)

`LISTEN_*` bits are in `constants.ts:72-81`; gating via `listens(node, bit)` (`index.ts:79-88`) — absent attribute = permissive. Example (`index.ts:323-335`):

```ts
const node = eventNodeOf(target, LISTEN_POINTER_UP);
if (node && transport.open) {
  const id = Number(node.getAttribute("data-pathland-id"));
  transport.send(encodePointerUp(id, e.clientX, e.clientY, secondary));
}
```

**Encoders** (`src/events.ts`) each produce a **self-contained single-opcode PLPL batch** with `CAT_EVENT`, guest→host flags `0x0000`, `sequence = 0` (`eventBatch`, `events.ts:41-57`). Signatures include:

```ts
encodePointerDown(target, x, y, flags?): Uint8Array        // events.ts:99
encodePointerUp(target, x, y, flags?): Uint8Array          // events.ts:109
encodeKeyDown(target, keyCode, modifiers, repeat?): Uint8Array  // events.ts:116
encodeValueChanged(target, value): Uint8Array              // events.ts:128
encodeTextChanged(target, text): Uint8Array                // events.ts:170
encodeScroll(target, offsetX, offsetY): Uint8Array         // events.ts:211
encodeNavigate(url): Uint8Array                            // events.ts:223
```

**Sending:** `Transport.send(bytes: Uint8Array): void` (`src/transport.ts:95-108`) — gated on `this.open` (`readyState === 1`, `transport.ts:91-93`), best-effort logs a description, then `this.ws.send(bytes)`. The node id rides only in the opcode's `A` field; the batch carries **no connection/stream/origin tag**.

---

## 5. WebSocket lifecycle

**One `Transport` instance per page**, constructed in `boot()` (`index.ts:145`) and started with `transport.start()` (`index.ts:170`). Class: `Transport` (`src/transport.ts:53`). Options: `TransportOptions` (`transport.ts:17-33`).

**URL construction** (`index.ts:146`) — includes the per-window id and the framework base:

```ts
url: `${location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss" : "ws"}://${location.host}${base}/ws?wid=${wid}`
```

**Per-window id (`wid`)** (`index.ts:120-143`): stored under `sessionStorage["pathland.wid"]`; generated with `crypto.randomUUID()` if absent; `isReload = wid != null`. It is deliberately **never** written into the page URL (the boot code strips any stale `?wid=` via `history.replaceState`, `index.ts:137-143`; `urlHadWid` records that a stale wid was present). Test: `test/wid.test.ts`.

**On open** (`index.ts:151-168`), ordered:
1. Send `encodeEnvironment(w, h, location.pathname)` **first** (`index.ts:154`) — seeds the server session's router.
2. `refreshFitSlots(renderer)` (`index.ts:158`).
3. If `isReload || urlHadWid`, send `encodeResync()` (`index.ts:164-167`).

**On reconnect** (`Transport.connect`'s `onopen`, `transport.ts:149-167`): `reconnected = this.attempt > 0`; re-baselines `expectedSequence = null`; calls `options.onOpen` (so environment is re-sent) and, **if reconnected, sends `encodeResync()`** (`transport.ts:163-166`).

**Sequence-gap recovery** (`transport.ts:229-237`): a guest→host batch whose `sequence` breaks the chain is **not applied**; the client sends `encodeResync()` and re-baselines on the next batch. `isSequenceGap`/`trackSequence` (`transport.ts:256-269`) ignore host→guest (`FLAG_HOST_TO_GUEST`) batches.

**Reconnect/backoff** (`transport.ts:185-192`): exponential `500ms * 2^attempt` capped at 30s, max 30 attempts. `onclose` → `scheduleReconnect` (`transport.ts:173-183`).

**Heartbeat** (`transport.ts:110-129`): `META::PING` every 5s; a no-activity watchdog (15s) force-closes a stalled-but-open socket → reconnect → resync.

**Version negotiation** (`transport.ts:219-223`): mismatched batch version → `location.reload()`.

**What happens on a full snapshot:** the client does **not** special-case it. A snapshot arrives as an ordinary batch and goes straight through `applyBatch`. Because `CREATE_NODE` reuses existing hydrated elements (`apply.ts:475-485`) and `INSERT_CHILD` skips already-present children (`apply.ts:522-528`), a replayed full tree **reconciles in place** rather than replacing the DOM. There is **no "clear the tree first"** step, and the server's resync **does not emit `META::RESET`** — `PathlandSession.resync()` calls `emitter.renderFull()` (`lib/java/pathland-server-core/.../PathlandSession.java:162-165`), and `Emitter.renderFull()` re-emits `TREE + PARAMETER` for the retained tree (`lib/java/pathland-view/.../emit/Emitter.java:164-179`). Consequence: **a `META::RESET` (if ever sent) would globally wipe every registered node**, while a resync replay leaves unrelated DOM (e.g. another stream's subtree) untouched but also would not remove stale nodes that vanished server-side. The hydration-aware reconcile is asserted in `test/apply.test.ts:530-589`.

---

## 6. Namespacing / a second independent opcode stream into a nested DOM region

**There is nothing today.** Concretely, the blockers a proxy-view feature must address:

1. **One flat, document-global id map.** `byId` is built from all `[data-pathland-id]` in the document (`index.ts:105`), and `DomRenderer.byId` is a `Map<number, Node>` with no stream/connection key (`apply.ts:311`). Ids from two servers collide. No `data-pathland-root`, no id prefixing, no per-element origin attribute exists anywhere.

2. **One connection.** `boot()` constructs a single `Transport` with a single `renderer` object (`index.ts:144-170`). There is no exported function to create a second renderer bound to a nested container; `index.ts` is a side-effect bootstrap with no exports of `boot`.

3. **Module-level shared state across any instances.** Even if you called `applyBatch` twice, these are module singletons:
   - `componentByNode` WeakMap (`apply.ts:100`)
   - `roleByNode` WeakMap (`apply.ts:307`)
   - `fitState` WeakMap + `ResizeObserver`s (`apply.ts:1342`)
   - `mediaState` WeakMap + global `setInterval` samplers (`apply.ts:1229-1236`)
   - `transitionsInjected` boolean (`apply.ts:695`)
   These are keyed by element, so they'd *mostly* coexist, but the whole-tree passes are not scoped.

4. **Whole-document queries and whole-tree passes.**
   - `applyLayout(r)` iterates **every** `byId` value and infers structure from `parentElement` (`apply.ts:162-303`). If stream B's root is nested under stream A's DOM, the layout pass would treat the cross-stream DOM parent/child as a protocol relationship (`apply.ts:289-302`).
   - `refreshFitSlots` and `dropFitBandRules` query the **whole document** (`apply.ts:1380`, `apply.ts:1505`).
   - `index.ts` hydration / media / fit scans are document-wide (`index.ts:105, 188, 200`).
   - The icon resolver scans the whole document (`icons.ts:28-34, 44-49`).

5. **Duplicate-id guard is global.** `insertAt`/`INSERT_CHILD` use `container.querySelector('[data-pathland-id="${op.b}"]')` (`apply.ts:527-528`) — with colliding ids across streams this mis-detects duplicates.

6. **`CMD_RESET` is global** (`apply.ts:386-401`): clears all of `byId`, i.e. would tear down both streams.

7. **Design tokens are global.** The default token sink writes `:root` custom properties into one `<style data-pathland-tokens>` in `document.head` (`createTokenSink`, `tokens.ts:65-98`; used at `apply.ts:808`). Two apps with different themes would fight over `--pl-*` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`.

8. **Events carry no origin.** Captured events resolve a raw numeric id and send it over the single socket (`index.ts:253` etc.); there is no per-stream routing tag, so a click in stream B's DOM would be sent to stream A's server if the ids overlap.

9. **Navigation is global.** `onRoute` calls `history.pushState` on the page URL, and `popstate` sends one NAVIGATE (`index.ts:218-242`) — a second embedded app would drive the same browser history.

10. **`wid` is one per window/tab** (`sessionStorage["pathland.wid"]`, `index.ts:127-133`), shared by whatever connections the page opens; there is no per-stream id.

### What *could* be reused today
`applyBatch`, `parseBatch`, `Transport`, `createElement`, and `childrenContainer` are all exported and take an explicit `DomRenderer`/`Batch` argument, so a proxy feature could in principle drive a second `{ byId }` over a nested region — but the module-level WeakMaps (`componentByNode`, `roleByNode`, `fitState`, `mediaState`), the global token sink/head queries, the document-wide event listeners in `boot()`, and the hard-coded root convention (id 1) mean that a correct second stream requires either (a) id **namespacing/remapping** at ingest and scoped event routing, or (b) refactoring the renderer into an instantiable class with per-instance state and a **root element scope**. ## 1. TREE opcode semantics and exact A/B/C layouts

**Spec table** — `spec/OPCODE.md:106-112`:

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CREATE_NODE` | `0x01` | nodeId | componentType (u16, low) | 0 | — |
| `DELETE_NODE` | `0x02` | nodeId | 0 | 0 | — |
| `INSERT_CHILD` | `0x03` | parentId | childId | index | — |
| `REMOVE_CHILD` | `0x04` | parentId | childId | 0 | — |
| `MOVE_CHILD` | `0x05` | parentId | childId | newIndex | — |

Append sentinel (`spec/OPCODE.md:110,112`): `index = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`). Constant `pub const APPEND: u32 = u32::MAX;` at `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs:772-773`, and command doc comments at `constants.rs:21-33`.

Exact opcode framing (`spec/OPCODE.md:38-65`, `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/opcode.rs:23-38`):
```
[Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]  // 16 B, little-endian, #[repr(C, packed)]
```

Golden bytes (`spec/CONFORMANCE.md:30-67`):
- `CREATE_NODE` id=1 VSTACK: `01 01 0000 01000000 10000000 00000000`
- `INSERT_CHILD` parent=0 child=1 APPEND: `01 03 0000 00000000 01000000 FFFFFFFF`
- `MOVE_CHILD` parent=1 child=2 newIndex=0: `01 05 0000 01000000 02000000 00000000`

**PARENT/CHILD encoding:** parent in `A`, child in `B`, index in `C`. `REMOVE_CHILD` uses `A=parent, B=child, C=0`. `DELETE_NODE` is node-only (`A`) and deletes the whole subtree (`spec/OPCODE.md:109`).

- The consumer discovers the root structurally as **"the single node without a parent."** `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-gtk/src/host.rs:277-280`:
  ```rust
  /// The root node: the single node without a parent.
  pub fn root(&self) -> Option<&HostNode> {
      self.nodes.values().find(|n| n.parent.is_none())
  }
  ```
  Same in the native flat-world host: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view-native/src/lib.rs:220-222`.
- **No `INSERT_CHILD` ever targets an implicit root.** Both emitters create the root with `CREATE_NODE` and never insert it into a parent:

- Node id `0` is **not reserved**. `HostNode::default()` itself is `id: 0` (`host.rs:68-81`), and `Node::id` is documented "0 until `assign_ids`" (`pathland-engine/src/node.rs:30`). Real emitters just start the root at **1** (see §2), so 0 is de-facto unused but not a sentinel.

## 3. PLPL network batch format, frames, and META commands

**Single wire format, one shared header** — `spec/OPCODE.md:660-684`; Rust `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport/src/batch.rs:86-108`; Java `FrameCodec.java:16-62, 337-343`; TS `plpl.ts:28-77`:

```
offset 0   magic    u32 LE = 0x504C504C ("PLPL")
offset 4   version  u16 LE = 1
offset 6   flags    u16 LE   (0x0000 guest→host, 0x0001 host→guest)
offset 8   sequence u32 LE   (per-stream monotonic; 0 for heartbeat/request)
offset 12  opcodeCount u32 LE
offset 16  opcodes: opcodeCount × 16 B
then       stringsLen u32 LE
then       string/arena bytes (length-prefixed entries `[u32 len][bytes]`)
```
Header is exactly 16 bytes: `BATCH_HEADER: usize = 16` (`batch.rs:8-9`). Magic/version/direction constants: `pathland-core-transport/src/lib.rs:80-91` (`BATCH_MAGIC=0x504C_504C`, `BATCH_VERSION=1`, `direction::GUEST_TO_HOST=0x0000`, `HOST_TO_GUEST=0x0001`); Java mirrors them at `FrameCodec.java:34-38`.

**Sections:** there is exactly **one trailing byte section**, whose meaning is codec-dependent — there is no multi-section "frames/events/strings" layout:
- **Self-contained frame codec** (`encode_frame`/`decode_frame`, `batch.rs:364-405`; Java `FrameCodec.encodeFrame/decodeFrame`, `FrameCodec.java:42-68`): the trailing bytes are the frame's **own string table**, and string/list operands use **relative offsets** into it. No prior state required.
- **Arena-delta codec** (`encode_batch`/`BatchEncoder`/`BatchDecoder`, `batch.rs:86-262`): the trailing bytes are only the **arena bytes appended since the previous batch**; string operands use **absolute arena offsets** and the consumer keeps a mirrored arena (`BatchDecoder`, `batch.rs:219-261`).
- **Host→guest events** reuse the same header with `flags=HOST_TO_GUEST`; `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` strings ride the same trailing section via **relative** offsets (`encode_events`/`decode_events`, `batch.rs:264-344`; `FrameCodec.encodeEvents`, `FrameCodec.java:187-245`).

**Frame delimiting:** a batch is the **network unit, not a frame**. There is no per-frame delimiter inside a batch; opcodes are delimited only by `opcodeCount`. Several emit-pass frames may coalesce into one batch (`spec/OPCODE.md:676-679`). On the shared-memory ring, frame boundaries are detected via the header `frameCount` (`spec/OPCODE.md:517-523`).
